item.title: Scandal-plagued 'Squad' rep cruises to Democratic nomination with no GOP roadblocks in view
item.description: Ayanna Pressley faces no challengers in the Massachusetts 7th district, but controversies over her husband's federal contract and finances loom large.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass., is officially the Democratic nominee for Massachusetts' 7th Congressional District after facing no challengers in Tuesday's primary.

But despite controversies involving Pressley's personal finances, her husband and racially charged remarks she's made, the "Squad member" will face no Republican candidate in the November general election.

Pressley's district encompasses roughly three-quarters of Boston, and the Cook Political Report ranks it as Solid Democrat. She was first elected to office in 2018, alongside Squad members Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich.

Although Pressley faced no competition in the primary or general election, she joined other Democratic candidates on the campaign trail, including state Rep. Tram Nguyen, a Democratic candidate for District 6. Like Pressley, Nguyen is calling to abolish ICE, implement Medicare for all and end all military aid to Israel.

ILHAN OMAR ON TRACK FOR FIFTH TERM AS MINNESOTA VOTERS MAINTAIN FAR-LEFT STREAK

Pressley also joined Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., on the campaign trail.

With no challengers from either political party, Pressley continued criticizing President Donald Trump and the conservative-majority Supreme Court this election cycle.

Following the Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, which held that creating a second majority-Black district constituted unconstitutional racial gerrymandering, Pressley accused the Trump administration of being "anti-Black" and "that would rather Black Americans pick cotton than pick the president, than pick their congressperson, than pick a senator."

MASSACHUSETTS SENATE CANDIDATES TRADE SHARP ATTACKS IN FIERY DEBATE AS INCUMBENT MARKEY SKIPS EVENT

A week before the primary, Pressley spoke at a campaign rally for Markey in which she said White supremacy is thriving under Trump's presidency.

"It is bigger than Trump," Pressley said. "Because whenever we do the work of ousting the occupant of the Oval Office, the Confederacy is still alive and well," Pressley said. "That’s all MAGA is. White supremacy is still alive and well. Anti-Blackness will still be alive and well."

VAN JONES WARNS FAR-LEFT SOCIALIST AGENDA IS 'REGRESSIVE' THREAT TO DEMOCRATIC PARTY

When introducing a bill in April aimed at providing relief to people facing eviction, Pressley called evictions "an act of violence."

However, critics pointed to Pressley's 2024 financial disclosure, which showed that she and her husband reported $8 million in assets from four Massachusetts rental properties.

In July, Pressley's husband, Conan Harris, also faced scrutiny after a company he partners with secured a $2 billion contract from the state to build a new courthouse in Massachusetts. John Barros, a key partner in CoJo Real Estate, divested from the company because of ethics concerns over how the contract was awarded.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Losing bidders for the project are now suing and pointing to Barros' departure from the company as evidence of wrongdoing.

However, Pressley is not accused of wrongdoing in the suit.

item.title: More than 180 Jewish entertainers rally behind actor Mark Ruffalo in protest letter
item.description: More than 180 Jewish artists signed a letter defending actor Mark Ruffalo after Paramount accused him of antisemitic tropes over his merger opposition.
item.content:encoded:
More than 180 Jewish entertainers and artists signed a letter Tuesday "proudly" voicing support for actor Mark Ruffalo after he was accused of antisemitism in his opposition to the proposed Warner Bros. Discovery-Paramount merger.

"We are Jewish artists, writers, creative professionals, faith leaders and thinkers who have, in response to the outrageous smear campaign against our respected colleague Mark Ruffalo, a simple message to share with the world: Enough!" the letter read, according to Variety. 

"Enough with the false and dangerous weaponization of charges of antisemitism against those who are brave enough to point out the obvious: that the assault on the Palestinian people and the assault on our liberties at home are deeply interconnected, and there is nothing antisemitic about recognizing that fact."

Ruffalo was previously accused of invoking "antisemitic tropes" by Paramount after the Marvel star shared a video from August of Safra Catz, an Oracle executive vice chair and Paramount board member, discussing technology Oracle used to assist Israel after the Oct. 7 Hamas terrorist attacks. 

JOHN CUSACK STANDS IN 'SOLIDARITY' WITH MARK RUFFALO AMID PARAMOUNT'S ANTISEMITISM ALLEGATION

He linked Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, the father of Paramount CEO David Ellison, to financing behind the proposed acquisition and suggested the merger would be used to push "oppression."

"These ‘really profoundly scary technologies’ will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you," Ruffalo said. "Look how she revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle."

The Jewish artists, who include Abbi Jacobson, Alex Winter, Gina Gershon, Ilana Glazer, James Schamus, Joel Coen, Larry Charles, Kate Berlant, Naomi Klein, Sarah Sherman, Jane Schoenbrun, Todd Haynes and Tony Kushner, denied this comment was antisemitic, claiming executives "themselves have explicitly linked to their support for the ongoing depredations being visited on the people of Palestine and their silencing of critics of those horrors."

"The AI road to WarnerMount runs through Gaza, and Ellison has often let us know the Orwellian world he has in store for us as he consolidates control over what we watch and how we watch it, knowing that as we watch he and his corrupt cohort will always be watching us," the letter read.

JEWISH EDUCATORS FACE RAMPANT ANTISEMITISM IN TEACHERS UNIONS, NEW REPORT FINDS

The celebrities also argued that a majority of American Jews now believe that Israel committed war crimes against Gaza, with a significant portion believing Israel is guilty of genocide. They called for an end to "spurious charges of antisemitism" against people like Ruffalo.

"Pointing out the crucial connections between what is happening in Gaza and what is happening in Hollywood is the exact opposite of antisemitism. It is, for us, the very essence of Jewish ethical duty," the letter read.

Fox News Digital reached out to Ruffalo's representatives for comment.

Ruffalo previously denied pushing antisemitism in a statement to Fox News Digital after Paramount's original condemnation.

MS RACHEL CONFRONTED ON ACCUSING ISRAEL OF 'GENOCIDE' IN PARK INTERACTION WITH PODCASTER

"The accusation that I am antisemitic is appalling and fundamentally dishonest," Ruffalo said. "Criticizing the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticizing Jewish people."

Ruffalo continued to receive backlash after a group of nearly 1,000 industry insiders, calling itself The Brigade, released a statement condemning the actor last week.

"This is not commentary on a merger. It is not a criticism of a government. It is simple antisemitism, where Jewish executives are portrayed as a secretive and powerful wealth-hoarding elite delighting in mass death," the statement read.

Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party’s Jewish engagement chair, told Fox News Digital Thursday that Ruffalo’s prominence in the opposition to the merger reflected Hollywood’s liberal political activism, while praising The Brigade for challenging him.

"Ruffalo as an anti-merger spokesman is an odd choice given his extremist rhetoric that has completely discredited him with rational people," Barcohana said.

"He is an activist more than an actor (indeed maybe that’s one in the same). I applaud The Brigade for organizing an oppositional force against the explosion of antisemitism within Hollywood and standing up to Ruffalo’s Israel Derangement Syndrome."

item.title: Colts GM Chris Ballard rips NFL players returning to college football: 'Stupidest s--- I’ve ever heard'
item.description: Colts GM Chris Ballard called NFL players seeking college football eligibility the "stupidest" thing he's ever heard as a Baton Rouge hearing looms.
item.content:encoded:
College sports have taken some strange turns in recent years, but they may have reached a new level of absurdity with professional football players attempting to return to the college ranks.

This is still being worked out in courts as players battle for a fifth year of college eligibility.

But one person who is definitely not on their side is Indianapolis Colts general manager Chris Ballard.

NFL TO NCAA? COURTROOM CHAOS IS GIVING PRO ATHLETES A BIZARRE PATH BACK TO COLLEGE, AND IT'S ONLY JUST BEGUN

According to CBS Sports, none of the Colts' players are among those trying to go all Rodney Dangerfield and head back to school. But if they did, they may want to reconsider, because they won't be getting any support from him on the matter.

"No," Ballard said after being asked if any players had talked to him about moving back to the collegiate ranks. "It's the stupidest s--- I've ever heard. I'm sorry. I know I'll catch crap for this. Your entire life, you fight to get up to the NFL, but now we're gonna go back. OK, that makes a lot of freaking sense."

Well, when you put it that way...

This comes after LSU brought in some players who had previously played for head coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss. The players in question had been signed to NFL teams before attempting to resume their college careers.

LSU ALUM BEN MCDONALD SAYS HE DOESN'T AGREE WITH NFL-TO-COLLEGE RETURNS, BUT UNDERSTANDS WHY COACHES WANT THEM

The SEC and the Big Ten have both put rules in place banning players who have appeared on professional rosters from returning to college.

However, a hearing is scheduled for Thursday in Baton Rouge that will take a look at the SEC's ban on former professionals.

item.title: DOJ lawsuit targets alleged school ‘secret gender transitions’ policies that keep parents in the dark
item.description: The DOJ lawsuit against Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools alleges "secret" gender transition plans locked parents out, violating FERPA and PPRA.
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Justice (DOJ) is investigating other school districts and contemplating additional lawsuits over alleged violations of federal parental rights laws, Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon told Fox News Digital Tuesday, calling the DOJ's newly filed "first-of-its-kind" case against Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools the "first of many."

The DOJ sued Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools (KCKPS) Tuesday, alleging the district violated the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA) with a district policy that facilitates "secret gender transitions" for students at school without their parents’ knowledge or consent.

"No, we're not waiting. What we do is we ask for documents, we investigate and then we try to resolve cases with school districts. And if we cannot, then we file lawsuits. And, so, there are many other lawsuits contemplated here and other investigations that are ongoing," Dhillon said when asked whether DOJ would wait for the Kansas case to conclude before pursuing other districts.

Dhillon declined to identify the other districts under investigation, saying she did not want to prejudge the outcomes.

EXCLUSIVE: HOUSE COMMITTEE PROBES CHICAGO PUBLIC SCHOOLS OVER HIDING 'GENDER AFFIRMATION' FROM PARENTS

"This is a really important lawsuit for us. And the point I wanted to emphasize is that it's the first of many," she said.

The DOJ lawsuit against KCKPS centers on internal guidance for transgender and gender non-conforming students. The DOJ alleges the district has used versions of the guidance since 2017.

Under the guidance described in the complaint, students can ask that their parents be excluded from school planning meetings and that their transgender or gender non-conforming status not be disclosed to their parents. The resulting written plans can address names, pronouns, school records, restroom and locker room use, sports and other accommodations.

Asked about KCKPS’ assertion that it complies with federal law, Dhillon rejected the district’s position.

FIRST ON FOX: SCHOOL LIED, HID DAUGHTER'S GENDER TRANSITION UNDER DISTRICT POLICY, PARENTS ALLEGE

"Well, I think you can get that from the complaint, but they had secret gender transition plans that locked parents out of knowing what was being asked of their children. So, I obviously completely reject that," Dhillon said.

KCKPS disputed DOJ’s allegations Tuesday in a news release.

"Contrary to the allegations in the complaint, the district maintains that it is in full compliance with FERPA and PPRA and is disappointed by the DOJ’s decision to file the lawsuit," the release read.

The district said it would respond through the federal court process and would not comment further while the litigation is pending.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION THREATENS KANAS SCHOOL DISTRICT FUNDING OVER TRANSGEDNER STUDENT POLICY

The DOJ argues the written plans constitute education records under FERPA and that excluding parents can prevent them from exercising their rights to inspect and challenge those records.

The government separately alleges the district violates PPRA by allowing students to participate in meetings and evaluations that can reveal sensitive information without prior written parental consent.

The Department of Education opened a FERPA investigation into KCKPS in August 2025.

The federal government advised the district Aug. 12 that its guidance violated FERPA and PPRA, and the complaint states the government ultimately determined KCKPS would not voluntarily comply.

The DOJ is asking a federal court to declare the district’s practices unlawful and prohibit enforcement of the guidance or similar policies that violate FERPA or PPRA.

Dhillon said the DOJ intends to pursue potential violations elsewhere.

"But I want there to be a very clear message to every school district in the United States. They are on notice that if they violate FERPA and PPRA, the United States Department of Justice stands ready to protect the rights of parents and the rights to pupils to privacy, dignity and parental rights in determining how children are educated in the United States," Dhillon said.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Kansas referred questions about the lawsuit to the DOJ’s Office of Public Affairs.

item.title: Former Florida governor hopeful hauled out of county meeting after protesting Israel investments
item.description: James Fischback was forcibly removed from a Miami-Dade commissioners meeting after protesting the county's raised investment limit in Israel bonds.
item.content:encoded:
James Fischback, a former Florida gubernatorial candidate and controversial political figure, was forcibly removed from a Miami-Dade Board of County Commissioners meeting Tuesday afternoon after protesting the county's expanded investment in Israel-backed bonds.

"Do you serve the people of Hialeah or of Haifa? Do you serve the people of Aventura or of Tel Aviv? Do you serve the people of South Miami or of Jerusalem? This money should be invested here in this community. It should be invested in Miami-Dade County," he added before officers escorted him from the room.

The confrontation comes after the county voted earlier this summer to raise its investment cap with Israel from 3% to 5% of its portfolio — a move that allows it invest upwards of about $400 million to $450 million. The change has drawn opposition from figures like Fischback critical of using public funds to invest in Israel as the war in Gaza continues to fuel political divisions in the U.S. It has also provided Fischback a platform to continue his opposition to U.S.-Israel ties.

ANTISEMITISM FIGHT EXPLODES IN FLORIDA AS VOTERS HEAD TO THE POLLS: 'POLITICAL POGROM'

"What this is about, very simply, is whom do you serve?" Fischback said.

Fischback, a Republican, has garnered national attention for his views on race and has developed a reputation for confrontational public appearances.

Fischback was among the 11 GOP candidates seeking to replace outgoing Gov. Ron DeSantis. He garnered 10.4% of the vote in the Aug. 18 primary but drew national attention for a series of inflammatory on-camera moments.

In one such case, he repeatedly called Rep. Byron Donalds, the frontrunner, eventual nominee and one of the only Black Republicans in Congress, a "slave" repeatedly at a news conference.

"Byron Donalds is a slave. I’m sorry, he’s a slave. He is a slave to his donors. He is a slave to the corporate interests, to the tech bros that want to turn our state into, in his own words, a financial capital," Fischback said.

He would later shout a similar phrase at Donalds directly, catching Donalds on the way back to his car with a megaphone and a throng of supporters.

"You’re a DEI hire. You’re a slave. Go back to New York," Fischback yelled.

JOSH SHAPIRO WARNS THAT ATTACKS ON AIPAC ARE BEING USED TO 'SILENCE CERTAIN VOTERS'

Fischback's comments on Tuesday weren't the only ones that expressed outrage over the portfolio change.

Other members of the public who expressed concern about the change voiced disappointment that the county would put public investment dollars behind Israel, given the politically charged atmosphere around the topic of its relations with the U.S.

Another woman who identified herself as Ivar Fandel walked to the podium wearing a "let Gaza live" shirt.

"Item 5B does exist in the context of a budget crisis as well as a genocide against Palestinians in Gaza at the hands of Israel," Fandel said, referring to the agenda item discussing the county's change.

During his campaign, Fischback positioned himself as one of the only Republican candidates to decline contributions from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC). He also pledged to divest from Israel-backed bonds.

"Florida has a specific policy. You’re not allowed to use taxpayer funds to buy foreign government bonds, with one exception: Israel. And so my premise is, first principles, we should not be lending taxpayer pensioner money to any foreign government," Fischback said in an interview with the American Conservative.

He also blasted several candidates, including Donalds, for what he characterized as "singular allegiance" to Israel.

HUCKABEE WARNS OF 'BIBLICAL IGNORANCE' AS HE DEFENDS CONSERVATIVE SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"I think people like Randy Fine and other AIPAC politicians have a singular allegiance. And that allegiance is to the best interests of Israel. The idea of saying ‘I am running to represent a foreign country’s interest in the United States Congress’ is preposterous. They’re buying allegiance," Fischback said in a post to X.

Fischback did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Fox News Digital.

item.title: WWE Crown Jewel set for November as company rounds out 2026 calendar
item.description: WWE Crown Jewel returns to Saudi Arabia on Nov. 7, setting the stage for a potential blockbuster WrestleMania rematch of Roman Reigns vs. CM Punk.
item.content:encoded:
WWE announced Tuesday that Crown Jewel was back on the premium live event calendar.

Crown Jewel will take place on Nov. 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD, furthering the partnership between WWE and Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority. Before the announcement, it was unclear whether Crown Jewel would take place in 2026.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

It will be the second time in the event’s history that it is held in Saudi Arabia. The first one in 2024 took place there, while the second one was held in Perth, Australia, last year.

Crown Jewel is one of the more unique premium live events of the year. It will feature the men’s and women’s champions of the Raw and SmackDown brands going up against each other, respectively, for the Crown Jewel Championship and the Crown Jewel ring.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

Cody Rhodes defeated Gunther and Seth Rollins beat Rhodes on the men’s side in the last two years. Liv Morgan defeated Nia Jax in 2024 and Stephanie Vaquer took care of Tiffany Stratton last year on the women’s side.

Plans could very well change for this year’s show but if the event were to begin tomorrow Roman Reigns would battle CM Punk in a WrestleMania 42 rematch for the men and Liv Morgan would take on Chelsea Green for the women. It’s definitely a long way to go for these champions to keep their titles going into Crown Jewel, but not impossible.

Punk is facing challenges from four members of SmackDown – Rhodes, Kevin Owens, Sami Zayn and Randy Orton, and could very well lose the belt at any time. Reigns has a matchup with Penta in Mexico City later this month to defend his title, but LA Knight is also nipping at his heels to get a shot at the championship.

Morgan has come under fire from fellow wrestlers for not being a fighting champion. However, she defeated Iyo Sky at SummerSlam. She has Vaquer and Becky Lynch gunning for her gold as well. Green has been injured as of late and might have to take care of Jax to get through to the next chapter of her reign.

WWE now has Sunday Night's Main Event, Money in the Bank, Crown Jewel, Survivor Series: WarGames and Wrestlepalooza: Perth on the calendar for the latter part of the year.

item.title: Rosie O’Donnell rants that Trump-era ICE facilities are concentration camps where inmates are raped
item.description: Rosie O'Donnell compared ICE detention facilities to concentration camps in Nazi Germany and suggested Dolly Parton should run the world instead.
item.content:encoded:
Actress Rosie O’Donnell compared ICE facilities to concentration camps in Nazi Germany in a video she posted on TikTok Friday.

In a TikTok titled, "Friday Ramble," O'Donnell discussed a variety of topics, including the recent death of country music legend Dolly Parton, before launching into criticism of the Trump administration.

"We all vowed ‘Never Again,’ remember?" she said in the TikTok video, referencing the Holocaust. She noted that people even today are shocked at how Germans allowed fascism to take over before claiming fascism is in full swing in the United States.

"We’re making concentration camps. … We’re rounding up people without a warrant. We’re raping children in detention, in ICE detention. They’re all getting pregnant," she said. "And they’re separated, males and females. Who has access to those girls? What happens to their babies? What do they do with them? There are big questions."

DEMOCRAT COMPARES ICE TO 'DOMESTIC TERRORISTS' AS 111 HOUSE DEMS DEMAND TEXAS DETENTION CENTER CLOSE

The fierce anti-Trump critic then launched into an attack on the president, saying his supporters were in denial. 

"He doesn't care about you one bit. This is not a president for all people. This is a president for people like him," she said of Trump in the same video. "White powerful men, where women are disregarded in that equation usually. It’s the White men, it’s patriarchy running the world and it’s deadly.

"We need people like Dolly Parton to run the world," she suggested. "People with a heart."

O'Donnell has a long history of condemning Trump and his administration.

ROSIE O'DONNELL HAMMERS TRUMP REPEATEDLY IN KIMMEL GUEST-HOST GIG AS WHITE HOUSE FIRES BACK

In July 2025, she made similar comparisons between ICE and Nazi Germany, saying, "I think Americans should stand up and say, ‘No way. You’re not going to silence us. You don’t have the right to silence us. You never did. And you never will. We, the people, have the right to speak up against atrocities which are happening on a daily basis.’ ICE, his own personal Gestapo — what will it take, America? What will it take?" she asked.

"He’s gonna arrest every artist that disagrees with him, and pretty much every artist does. Whether or not they’re brave enough to say it is another thing."

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis called O'Donnell's comments "gross" in a statement to Fox News Digital, providing a list of arrests made by ICE yesterday of illegal aliens accused of violent crimes like strangulation, battery and child molestation.

"This is gross. These types of comparisons of ICE to Nazis are contributing to our brave law enforcement officers facing a more than 1,300% increase in assaults against them and an 8,000% increase in death threats. Would Rosie O’Donnell want these thugs for neighbors?" Bis asked.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

O'Donnell recently wrapped up guest-hosting fellow Trump critic Jimmy Kimmel's late-night show, where she called Trump, "orange Voldemort."

Media analyst and Fox News contributor Joe Concha said O'Donnell's rants are evidence of "severe Trump Derangement Syndrome."

"It shows that there is a disturbing segment of the population who are no different from Rosie: STDS sufferers… Severe. Trump. Derangement. Syndrome," Concha told Fox News Digital. "And their lives revolve around hating the president. So there is an audience for this stuff, albeit a deranged audience.  It just shows you how much Kimmel is suffering from STDS by selecting a deranged Rosie to host in his place. Why not get Sebastian Maniscalco? Dave Chappelle? People who actually make people laugh?  She was chosen not because she’s a good comic or host, but because she would try to stick it to Trump. And it was as cringe-worthy and sad as it gets."

item.title: Arte Moreno era officially over as Angels sell to Rams owner Stan Kroenke for $4B
item.description: Stan Kroenke agreed to buy the Angels from Arte Moreno for north of $4 billion, making it the single most expensive franchise sale in MLB history.
item.content:encoded:
Calling all Angels fans: The Arte Moreno era is officially over. After two decades of blown leads, wasted talent, and front-office chaos, Moreno has finally done what Halos fans have begged him to do for years:

Arte finally agreed to sell the team.

Billionaire Stan Kroenke, owner of the Rams, Nuggets and Avalanche, swooped in Tuesday to rescue the Angels from baseball’s purgatory. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment is buying the franchise for $4 billion — making it the most expensive sale in Major League Baseball history.

PADRES STRIKE DEAL TO SELL TO INVESTOR GROUP LED BY PRIVATE EQUITY BILLIONAIRE, VOWS WORLD SERIES CHAMPIONSHIP

"The Angels are a storied franchise anchored in a great market," Kroenke announced in a statement.

"We look forward to an exciting future with the Angels organization."

The price tag eclipses the Padres’ $3.9 billion record and crushes Steve Cohen’s $2.4 billion purchase of the Mets.

MLB ALL-STAR MIKE TROUT SHUTS DOWN IDEA OF LEAVING LA, SAYS DOUBTERS FUEL PUSH TO GET ANGELS BACK TO PLAYOFFS

Across American sports, it matches Mat Ishbia’s $4 billion Phoenix Suns takeover, trailing only the Denver Broncos ($4.65 billion) and Washington Commanders ($6.05 billion).

Moreno bought the club in 2003 for $184 million, right after its lone World Series title. He released a statement on the sale:

"The Moreno Family has been honored to steward the Angels for 23 years, and we believe with KSE’s experience and success they are the best next owner for the franchise.

"The Angels organization looks forward to continuing its commitment to the fans, our employees, the players and our business partners."

KHOSLA FAMILY REACHES DEAL TO BUY SUPER BOWL CHAMPION SEAHAWKS FOR NFL-RECORD PRICE: REPORT

The Halos haven't made the playoffs since 2014, the longest active postseason drought in baseball.

Around baseball, the Halos became an absolute punchline for squandering the prime years of Mike Trout and Shohei Ohtani on the exact same roster. Ohtani eventually left, crossing town to win a World Series with the Dodgers, while Trout stayed behind, loyal to a fault.

Under Moreno, the organization handed out disastrous contracts to aging stars like Albert Pujols, Josh Hamilton and Anthony Rendon, let the farm system rot, and constantly burned through leadership, most recently firing GM Perry Minasian in June.

Then came the cruelest tease of all: Moreno’s 2023 decision to explore a sale, only to abruptly yank the team off the market citing "unfinished business."

Through every bad contract and lost season, Halos fans kept packing Angel Stadium, proving how deeply beloved this team remains.

That loyalty is why Tuesday turned into an impromptu party outside Angel Stadium.

Hours before first pitch against the Yankees, fans gathered to celebrate Arte’s exit, like they’d just won a World Series.

The Angels enter a new era under Kroenke, whose championship empire spans the Super Bowl-winning Rams, NBA champion Nuggets and Stanley Cup champion Avalanche.

The deal won't officially close until early 2027, pending MLB approval, but the Moreno era is finished.

item.title: Tiger Woods set for plea change hearing after DUI arrest following Florida rollover crash
item.description: Tiger Woods is set for a change of plea hearing Wednesday in Martin County after his DUI arrest following a rollover crash near his Florida home.
item.content:encoded:
Five-time Masters champion Tiger Woods is expected to arrive at a Florida court Wednesday for a hearing on a possible plea change in his DUI case, court records show. The case stems from a rollover crash on Jupiter Island, Florida, in March more than five months ago.

A photo from WPTV at the time showed what was reportedly an SUV registered to Woods lying on its driver’s side. Authorities found Woods at the crash scene in Martin County, Florida, roughly 40 miles outside West Palm Beach. An arrest affidavit said Woods did not pass a field sobriety test and had prescription painkillers in his pocket.

In the aftermath of the crash, Woods announced he would take some time away from the public eye and explore personal recovery treatment options.

Woods initially entered not guilty pleas to misdemeanor counts of driving under the influence and refusing to submit to testing.

He also received a citation for careless driving and had been scheduled to make an appearance in court on Sept. 8. However, a court notice filed Tuesday moved Woods’ appearance up to Wednesday morning.

JUDGE APPROVES TIGER WOODS' HOSPITAL RECORDS RELEASE TO PROSECUTORS AFTER FLORIDA CAR CRASH

The 15-time major champion’s plea conference is scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. Wednesday at the Martin County Courthouse. It remains unclear whether Woods plans to change his plea or whether his attorneys have reached a plea agreement with prosecutors.

Fox News Digital attempted to contact Woods’ legal team about the latest development, but did not immediately receive a response.

The rollover added to a series of crashes involving Woods and created another obstacle in his latest comeback bid after years of injuries.

TIGER WOODS MAKES FIRST PUBLIC APPEARANCE SINCE DUI, REHAB STINT AS PGA TOUR ANNOUNCES SWEEPING CHANGES

Woods was seriously injured in a February 2021 single-vehicle crash outside Los Angeles. His SUV rolled several times, leaving him trapped inside the vehicle.

Emergency surgery treated "open fractures" in Woods’ lower right leg. Doctors placed a rod in his tibia and inserted screws and pins in his foot and ankle. He remains hospitalized for several weeks following the procedure.

Though Woods remains away from competition, he has continued to follow the game closely. On Sunday, he congratulated Scottie Scheffler on social media after the current world No. 1 won the Tour Championship, secured his second FedEx Cup title and passed Woods atop the PGA Tour’s career earnings list.

"Three wins, five runner-ups and finishing the season No. 1. Those are some numbers to be proud of," Woods wrote in a post to X. "Incredible consistency all season long. Congrats on a historic season, Scottie."

item.title: Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, reveals what 'Friends' star is really like behind closed doors

item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend, Jim Curtis, is offering a rare glimpse into their relationship, from how they handle disagreements to what the actress is really like behind closed doors.

"It's going really well. My experience of her is so grounded and so open and caring and kind and loving," he gushed during a recent appearance on "The Jamie Kern Lima Show" podcast.

JENNIFER ANISTON'S BOYFRIEND FLAUNTS STEAMY ROMANCE IN RARE PDA-PACKED PHOTOS

The couple, who have been linked for more than a year, have largely kept their relationship private. But Curtis offered a candid look at their life together, including how they handle disagreements and what it means to be welcomed into Aniston’s close-knit inner circle.

"She uses words like ‘my love.’ … She has this group of best friends that are like family," he said.

"I feel incredibly blessed to be part and welcomed into that family, and I feel blessed to be in a relationship with someone that is so open-hearted."

Curtis also praised Aniston for staying grounded despite her fame.

JENNIFER ANISTON OFFERS RARE PEEK INTO HOLIDAY CELEBRATIONS WITH BOYFRIEND JIM CURTIS

"Inclusive. Isn't that a beautiful thing? We're really a model for how we can all be in this world, right?" Curtis said.

He said Aniston stands out because she stays true to herself despite her Hollywood fame.

"She has an opportunity. Like, you would understand if she was less so. … Right? I think that she is a real example of stepping into possibility, as she came from ... living in New York and New Jersey, and, like, there was … this kind of household name and retained herself."

Curtis also got candid about what happens when the couple disagrees.

JASON ALDEAN SAYS HE AND WIFE BRITTANY ‘AGREE TO DISAGREE’ AFTER 11 YEARS OF MARRIAGE AS THEY TEAM UP FOR DUET

The pair, he revealed, lean on relationship tools such as communication, acceptance and understanding instead of letting disagreements escalate.

The couple first sparked romance rumors in July 2025 after they were spotted aboard a yacht off Mallorca, Spain.

item.title: Van Jones calls out El-Sayed for ‘insane’ belief that he’s ‘smarter than Barack Obama’ on Israel policy
item.description: Van Jones called Abdul El-Sayed's total arms embargo stance against Israel "insane" and questioned whether he thinks he's smarter than Barack Obama.
item.content:encoded:
CNN host and former advisor to President Barack Obama Van Jones questioned if Michigan Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed thought he was "smarter than Barack Obama" on foreign policy in fiery comments discussing the "dangerous" beliefs held by many progressive figures in the Democratic Party.

El-Sayed, a vocal critic of Israel and former CNN commentator, has been embroiled in political controversies regarding his stance toward Israel and his relationship with a famous left-wing livestreamer, Hasan Piker. 

In late August, Jones appeared on the "Ask Haviv Anything" podcast, where he addressed how the long and historic alliance between Black and Jewish Americans has recently fractured. He went on to criticize El-Sayed over his stance on Israel, saying, "his positions on Israel and foreign policy are insane."

"Look, some Democrats are going to say that we should condition military aid. That, you know, 'Israel's gone too far in Gaza and in the West Bank and in Lebanon. We're going to put some conditions on you.' I think that's a defensible position if you're a Democrat," he said. "That's not Abdul's position."

VAN JONES WARNS FAR-LEFT SOCIALIST AGENDA IS 'REGRESSIVE' THREAT TO DEMOCRATIC PARTY

"I can get why you would say, ‘No more aid, they got to pay their own way.' That’s not Abdul’s position. Abdul’s position is a total and complete arms embargo against the state of Israel, including defensive weapons. That’s an insane position," Jones continued. "That says, if Israel wants to pay for interceptors to stop a rocket coming from Iran or coming from Hezbollah or coming from Hamas, an interceptor, we should deny them the right to buy the interceptors to knock down rockets going at Israeli children, women, men, babies. That’s an insane position."

Jones went on to question if El-Sayed believed he was wiser than Obama on U.S. policy toward Israel.

"And by the way, it offends me because that’s — you know, Barack Obama was a part of creating that Iron Dome. Barack Obama was a part of creating those interceptors. Barack Obama thought that the Israeli people were in such a tough neighborhood, they needed to be able to knock down rockets," Jones recalled. "So you’re telling me you’re smarter than Barack Obama? You have better ideas about foreign policy than Barack Obama? And you want to de-plug and defund and take away Israel’s — half the world’s Jews'— ability to defend themselves? That's an insane position."

"The fact that people are having a hard time figuring out what to do about it, I find alarming," he continued. "This is not acceptable."

MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE CONFRONTED REPEATEDLY OVER ISRAEL’S RIGHT TO EXIST, DEFUNDING THE POLICE

Julian Epstein, a Democratic consultant and former chief counsel to the House Judiciary Committee, argued that El-Sayed has a long pattern of concerning positions and statements.

"Bless Van Jones' heart, I agree with him," Epstein said in comments to Fox News Digital. "To my mind, El Sayed is clearly aligned with the Muslim Brotherhood propaganda machine that gives a pass to the butchering of millions of Arabs by extremist Islamist overlords in the Middle East while slandering Israel with lies like a 'apartheid' and 'genocide' to justify the exterminationist and racist ideology that has always driven this conflict."

Theo Wold, former assistant attorney general and former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy under President Donald Trump warned that El-Sayed is part of a generational phenomenon of migrant populations taking up radical positions as they gain political power.

"Abdul El-Sayed is not a one-off. He’s the avatar of the rising generation of Third World immigrants who were resettled in the United States over the last thirty years," Wold said. "Visit a high school classroom in Anaheim or Queens, and you’re likely to encounter similar radical claptrap. El-Sayed’s foreign policy is more ‘global south’ than it is American. His messaging is so radically foreign to American ears because it’s just that: radical and foreign. And increasingly, that’s what the post-American, pro-Antifa Democrat Party has become, as well."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Jesse Arm, a Manhattan Institute vice president and pollster who was born in Michigan, said that Van Jones deserved credit "for drawing a clear and principled line" on the issue, arguing that Black Democrats are being sidelined by the radical wing of their party.

"Jones’s frustration reflects a larger struggle within the Democratic Party. Reasonable liberals like him — especially those rooted in the African American community —recognize that they are losing control of a party they helped build. As the Democratic coalition becomes Whiter, richer, and more ideologically extreme, the preferences of most Black voters are increasingly subordinated to those of the party’s new activist base," he added further. "Fringe extremists like El-Sayed and his top campaign surrogate, the racist streamer Hasan Piker, are seeking to marginalize and silence those voters, replacing the politics of the Black church with the politics of the campus encampment. There's a reason El-Sayed got crushed with African Americans in Michigan's Democratic primary, losing three-quarters of the Black vote to his more mainstream opponent."

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed's campaign about Van Jones' statements and did not receive an immediate reply.

item.title: Chiefs heiress Gracie Hunt wrestles the franchise's attention back from Taylor Swift with engagement party
item.description: Gracie Hunt and fiancé Derek celebrated their engagement party at Arrowhead Stadium, the place where the Kansas City Chiefs heiress' love story began.
item.content:encoded:
Move over Taylor Swift, Kansas City Chiefs heiress Gracie Hunt has some headlines of her own to make. The attention surrounding the singer's wedding to Travis Kelce this offseason was nice, but it's back to business.

The offseason is over, the NFL regular season kicks off next week and the face of the front office has engagement party content to share. This is about love. This is about football. And this is about the future of the franchise.

The engagement party debrief at the place they met tells the story for Gracie and her fiancé, Derek, son of former Chiefs quarterback Trent Green, who popped the question back in April.

TRAVIS KELCE CALLS MARRYING TAYLOR SWIFT AT MADISON SQUARE GARDEN 'THE BEST NIGHT OF MY LIFE'

The Chief's heiress wrote, "Of all the places, all the moments—God wrote our story to begin right here. So grateful to have come back to this stadium engaged, surrounded by the people we love. 🤍"

Exactly. Their story had to start at Arrowhead Stadium. She has a franchise to lead one day and whoever she marries has to be prepared for what that takes.

I don't mean to suggest that there's some rift between Tay Tay and Gracie. For all I know, they get along fine. This isn't personal. This is about making sure the Chiefs Kingdom knows who will be there long term.

CHIEFS HEIRESS GRACIE HUNT DUMPS OUT WORLD CUP CONTENT, SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM LOVES HER FINGER POINT & FAST FOOD

When Travis Kelce calls it quits, the Taylor Swift sightings at Chiefs games will become rare at best. She'll show up for the Ring of Honor ceremony and whenever else the tight end is honored, but not much else.

The same can't be said for Gracie Hunt. She's been there for everything and, in one way or another, will be going forward. She doesn't have the luxury of just showing up on Sunday.

CHIEFS COACH ANDY REID HAS A BLUNT RESPONSE TO EVERYONE FREAKING OUT OVER TRAVIS KELCE'S DAD BOD

There are no off days, especially during the season. If she's not in attendance, she'll need to make sure to recognize all franchise-related activities, as she did on draft day this year in her red bikini.

It's part of what goes along with being the heiress of an NFL franchise. She doesn’t need to rent a stadium for any events, they already have one.

item.title: Ohio woman learns fate in fatal dragging of driver who climbed onto her hood in road rage death
item.description: Danielle Henry was driving a stolen car after shoplifting at a Kroger in Westerville when a parking lot fender bender turned into a fatal encounter.
item.content:encoded:
An Ohio woman who dragged a DoorDash driver to his death following a fender bender in a grocery store parking lot was sentenced last week to up to 5½ years in prison.

Danielle Henry was handed the sentence after pleading guilty last month to aggravated vehicular homicide in the death of 38-year-old Ibrahim Diakite, WBNS-TV reported.

Henry had just shoplifted and was driving a stolen car when she collided with Diakite in October 2025 at a Kroger parking lot in Westerville.

The incident escalated, authorities said, when Henry fled in her vehicle.

PREGNANT WOMAN DRIVING HOME FROM PRENATAL VISIT SHOT DURING ALLEGED ROAD RAGE ATTACK: POLICE

Diakite followed and pulled up in front of her at a stoplight. He got out and stopped in front of Henry's vehicle in an effort to prevent her from leaving. He then climbed onto the hood of the car.

Henry drove off and sped up to 45 mph before jerking the car. Diakite was pulled under the vehicle and dragged for about 300 to 600 feet before he was run over, authorities said.

TEXAS DOORDASH DRIVER GETS HIT BY A CAR FLEEING FROM POLICE AND STILL DELIVERS THE ORDER

Diakite was later pronounced dead at a hospital.

At the time of the road rage incident, Henry had several active warrants, for charges of theft, receiving stolen property and failure to comply with police.

"She was obviously willing to do whatever she could to keep from being caught by the police and showed herself to be a danger to the community," Westerville Police Chief Holly Murchland told the news outlet.

Henry will be required to serve at least four years, and her driver's license was permanently suspended.

item.title: CBS chief Bari Weiss' involvement in viral El-Sayed report sparks debate among critics
item.description: The involvement of CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss in a viral report about Dem hopeful Abdul El-Sayed's deleted 9/11 tweets sparks fierce debate.
item.content:encoded:
The alleged involvement of CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss in a report about Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has fueled a fiery debate on social media.

The network drew far-left outrage Monday for a report putting a spotlight on El-Sayed's deleted posts about 9/11 and linking them to the forthcoming 25th anniversary of the terrorist attack.

"As the nation prepares to mark 25 years since Sept. 11, 2001, Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan, may be facing the risk of renewed scrutiny and fresh political attack," CBS News wrote Monday.

CBS NEWS TAKES HEAT OVER REPORT ON DEM HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED'S NOW-DELETED 9/11 POSTS

Later that evening, Status News reported that Weiss "praised the story during the network's daily editorial meeting" and that she "personally directed that the headline be tweaked to specifically mention that El-Sayed had deleted tweets referencing the September 11 terrorist attacks."

Weiss' version of the headline, which was published, "Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed's deleted tweets on Sept. 11 attacks invite scrutiny of past remarks," provided context to the substance of the report. Fox News Digital learned the pre-Weiss headline originally read, "For Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, Sept. 11 commemoration invites scrutiny of past remarks."

SOCIALIST CANDIDATES CAN DELETE OLD POSTS, BUT THEY CAN'T ERASE THEIR RADICALISM

Many on the left viewed Weiss' involvement in the El-Sayed story as a "scandal."

"A major scandal for CBS," the liberal outlet MeidasTouch reacted on X.

"It should be a scandal that a major American news network is now led by an overt, hands-on, undisguised Islamophobe but... it isn't. Islamophobia has been normalized in our media, and in our country. Shamefully," Zeteo founder and former MSNBC host Mehdi Hasan wrote.

"Not a good look whatsoever," Democratic strategist and podcast host Dan Turrentine said.

"Democrats: CBS must not be invited/allowed to host any debate in which Dem candidate appears," former Washington Post columnist Jennifer Rubin declared on the liberal social media platform Bluesky. "The penalty for gutter racism and toadyism to a MAGA/fascist regime is that you do not get accorded treatment as a real news outlet. PERIOD."

Meanwhile, many conservatives laughed off the zealous reactions from the left and the report's findings about Weiss doing her job.

"So she’s the editor-in-chief?" National Review senior editor Charles C.W. Cooke reacted.

"How dare she improve the objective journalism of the entity she is responsible for," The Federalist editor-in-chief and Fox News contributor Mollie Hemingway replied.

"An editor does editing. News at 11," Washington Free Beacon reporter Chuck Ross quipped.

"Fascinated by the Bari Derangement Syndrome," GOP strategist Matt Whitlock reacted. "The Democrat candidate in the top Senate race in the country has been deleting tweets about how he feels about 9/11... After campaigning with a surrogate who said America deserved 9/11. Seems pretty newsworthy!"

CBS News did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The CBS report cited El-Sayed's deleted social media posts, including some from 2020 comparing the nearly 3,000 Americans killed on 9/11 to the death toll from the coronavirus pandemic. Another post from Sept. 11, 2021, first uncovered by The Washington Free Beacon, read, "Today, I mourn the 3K lives, 6K injuries, & infrastructural devastation in NYC, perpetuated ignorantly in the name of my faith. Tomorrow, I'll mourn ~1M lives, millions of injuries, & infrastructural devastation in 3 countries, perpetuated ignorantly in the name of my country."

UNEARTHED EL-SAYED ESSAY DRAWS EXPLOSIVE TRUMP-BIN LADEN PARALLEL: ‘RECRUITED, RADICALIZED AND REASSURED’

El-Sayed was confronted about his deleted posts by a local CBS News reporter on the campaign trail.

"What happened on 9/11 is a disaster. It was a terrible attack on our country," El-Sayed said. "And our responsibility is also to think about, how do we build an America where we are protecting our servicemen and women from being asked to fight in wars we have no business fighting in?"

A CBS News source familiar with the story previously shrugged off the criticism, telling Fox News Digital that reports about deleted social media posts from politicians are published "all the time."

item.title: Republicans turn on House GOP lawmaker accused of late-night texts, lavish gifts to female staffers
item.description: Several House Republicans joined Democrats to censure Chuck Edwards after an ethics probe found he created a hostile work environment for staffers.
item.content:encoded:
Nearly every House Republican joined all Democrats to admonish one of their own after a bombshell investigation found that the lawmaker had engaged in "unprofessional and inappropriate conduct" with his staff.

The House voted to censure Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., on a landslide 413 to 2 vote as Congress has grappled with multiple incidents of alleged sexual harassment and misconduct by lawmakers on both sides of the aisle. Only Edwards and Rep. Ralph Norman, R-S.C., voted against the resolution.

The censure vote on Tuesday comes on the heels of a bombshell House Ethics Committee report released last month that recommended Edwards be rebuked for "persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers."

BAD BOSSES ON CAPITOL HILL COULD FACE RECKONING UNDER NEW ANONYMOUS STAFFER REVIEW PLATFORM

The committee is chaired by Edwards' fellow Republican Rep. Michael Guest, R-Miss., but acts on a bipartisan basis to investigate lawmakers on both sides of the aisle.

Guest noted on the House floor that the investigation did not find evidence that Edwards engaged in sexual activity, nor did he explicitly proposition the staffers, but that his "conduct toward two young female staffers was inappropriate and violated rules prohibiting sexual harassment," and that it created a hostile work environment.

"The committee found that Representative Edwards was, at a minimum, blind to the reality and at worst dismissive of the impact his conduct had on the career and well-being of the women on his staff," Guest said.

REPLACEMENT GOP NOMINEE NAMED AFTER REP CHUCK EDWARDS DROPS RE-ELECTION BID

Ahead of the vote, Edwards told Fox News Digital, "They’ll make their argument, and I’ll make mine," and countered that the House Ethics Committee had abandoned "its own rules" in its handling of his case.

That report detailed lavish gifts, trips, and the reading of a poem to one of the staffers, going to a staffer's home to perform chores, late-night personal texts, and taking one of the staffers to a casino, among other interactions. He ended his bid for re-election two days after its release.

He disputed the report on the House floor — after apologizing to the pair of staffers at the center of the Ethics Committee’s probe, along with his wife and family — accusing the bipartisan panel of cherry-picking the context of the incidents to fit a specific narrative.

He challenged the censure vote at hand and contended that his regret over the situation was "not an admission of sexual harassment."

"Generosity is not sexual harassment. Caring deeply about the people with whom you've worked for years is not sexual harassment," Edwards said. "And conduct that is otherwise permissible does not automatically become misconduct, simply because enough individual moments are assembled together and viewed through the darkest possible ends."

CAPITOL SEX SCANDALS SPARK PUSH TO BAN HOUSE LAWMAKERS FROM SLEEPING WITH STAFFERS

Still, his arguments weren’t enough to dissuade his colleagues. Notably, the entirety of House Republican leadership voted for the resolution.

Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, D-N.M., who chairs the Democratic Women’s Caucus, contended that since Edwards "continues to show no remorse, it's obvious that Edwards refuses to understand sexual harassment or his abuse of power."

"If we don't take action today, there is no opportunity for these women to receive justice," Leger Fernández said.

Edwards became the 30th member of the House of Representatives to be censured, which carries the penalty of a public rebuke for his conduct but does not force him to resign from his seat.

It also comes as other members of the House have grappled with their colleagues’ conduct in recent months. Earlier this year, former Reps. Eric Swalwell and Tony Gonzales both resigned on the same day.

Swalwell resigned after being hit with allegations of rape and sexual assault, while Gonzales exited Congress after being accused of sexual misconduct with a former staffer, and after he admitted to having an affair with his former staffer, Regina Santos-Aviles, who later died by setting herself on fire.

Both faced the rare threat of expulsion.

item.title: Best hikes to try around Lubbock ahead of Texas Tech's week one matchup with Abilene Christian
item.description: Lubbock Lake Landmark, Buffalo Springs Lake, and Caprock Canyons State Park top the list of must-hike trails near the Texas Tech game this weekend.
item.content:encoded:
With week zero of the college football season in the books, we turn our attention to the main course: week one.

Dozens of college football games will be played this weekend in a ton of amazing cities across the country, and many of you will be making your way out to these venues to take in some of the action.

Much like with week zero, we here at OutKick OutDoors wanted to give you some of the best hiking spots in some of the most unique and picturesque destinations, and this weekend on the docket is Lubbock, Texas.

FIVE BEST HIKES IN TALLAHASSEE TO TRY AHEAD OF FLORIDA STATE AND NEW MEXICO STATE'S WEEK ZERO SHOWDOWN

The 12th-ranked Texas Tech Red Raiders will be taking on the Abilene Christian Wildcats, and if you are making the trip to see this game in person, chances are you are going to want to explore all the natural beauty that the area has to offer.

Much like with our week zero hiking spots highlight for Tallahassee, this one comes with a heat warning.

HIKING ETIQUETTE RULES THAT SHOULD BE COMMON SENSE BUT APPARENTLY NEED TO BE SPELLED OUT FOR SOME PEOPLE

West Texas in September is an oven, and it's a dry heat at that.

You won't sweat quite as much as you might in the Florida Panhandle, but that just means the dehydration will sneak up on you, so make sure you're staying hydrated and dress appropriately.

With all that said, let's unpack everything Lubbock has to offer.

Consider this one the "must do" for anyone not from the Lubbock area.

Lubbock Lake Landmark offers quintessential West Texas views and wide open spaces for a relatively easy hike.

The entire trail includes nearly five miles of hiking and sits right along the Yellowhouse Draw, combining mixed-grass prairies with an archeological dig site.

If you're into history, the trail takes you right past the excavation site and gives hikers a view of thousands of years of human occupation.

And if the combination of West Texas views and archeological history doesn't sell you on Lubbock Lake Landmark, here's the real kicker: admission is free!

You can't beat that price point.

If you're looking for less of a "touristy" destination, Dunbar Historical Lake is the pick.

The East Loop of the trail offers a two-mile hike that is a solid workout for beginning hikers, while the West Loop offers a more hilly, five-mile experience that will put your glutes and quads to the test.

The actual elevation changes and dirt trails all winding around a lake will challenge you while also giving you some great views of the natural beauty that Lubbock has to offer.

THESE ARE THE DEFINITIVE UNWRITTEN RULES OF CAMPGROUND ETIQUETTE EVERYONE SHOULD KNOW

If you're a mountain biker, this site has some added appeal for you as well, as the trail is super popular among the biking community.

Dunbar Historical Lake is super convenient to get to, sandwiched between several major thoroughfares, but it never feels too close to the urban sprawl.

I promise they won't all be lakes!

For anyone looking for the best scenery that Lubbock has to offer without venturing too far outside the city limits, Buffalo Springs Lake offers outstanding canyon and lake views.

The 1.7-mile nature trail built by the Llano Estacado Audubon Society is definitely something to write home about, as you start out on the bluffs before making your way down towards the shores of the lake.

Bird watchers will also get an added bonus, as there are plenty of different aviary species that call this park home.

One thing to note, the trails aren't super well-manicured nor are they regularly groomed, so this is an example of "roughing it" for a hike.

With that said, the trails are well worth it, and with the added camping, fishing, and water activities provided here, Buffalo Springs Lake should absolutely be on your list.

Are you looking for wilderness vibes without straying from the city? Mae Simmons Park has you covered.

You can get your fill of the Yellowhouse Canyon without ever having to leave the comfort of Lubbock at this local hidden gem.

Both hikers and mountain bikers swear by Mae Simmons Park, and the trail network offers great views and wild terrain that ditches the conventional walking paths of most city hikes.

Locals swear by this park, as hikers from the area give Mae Simmons Park high marks, and the Outer Loop Trail in particular is one worth checking out.

Consider this an option if you don't want to burn an entire half a day driving to enjoy the great outdoors.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

This last one is a bit off the beaten path, but I promise it's worth it.

For those of you making an extended stay in Lubbock, Caprock Canyons State Park is 90 miles outside the city limits, so make sure you dedicate a day for this one.

With that said, the trail is simply astounding.

Caprock Canyons offers 25 miles of trails, red-rock canyons, and challenging hikes for even the most seasoned veterans.

If you happen to be one of those veteran hikers, might I suggest the Haynes Ridge Overlook, a 2.3-mile trail that is a serious workout and features a 600-foot ascent with some of the best views in the entire state.

Wildlife lovers will have plenty to cheer about too, as the park boasts a large population of bison roaming throughout the area.

There are so many trails to pick from, it's almost like a "choose your own adventure" in hiking form, so load up the car and don't miss out on this stunner of a state park.

item.title: Conservative journalists fire back at Washington Post after report claiming Pentagon 'secretly installed' them
item.description: Rob Maness, Kurt Schlichter and Thomas Anderson fired back at The Washington Post over a report on Sunday suggesting they were "installed" by the Pentagon.
item.content:encoded:
Conservative journalists attacked The Washington Post for a report on Sunday suggesting they were "secretly installed" by the Pentagon to push pro-Trump administration narratives.

The article, written by Dan Lamothe and Tara Copp, suggested that former military members Rob Maness, Kurt Schlichter and Thomas Anderson were hired as "civilian employees" under the Pentagon, adding that each has supported Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and attacked critics of the Trump administration's military strategy.

"The Pentagon has secretly installed several conservative military veterans with large online followings in government roles, declining to disclose their assignments as they amplify Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's viewpoints and attack those who scrutinize the Trump administration, according to people familiar with the matter and corroborating material," the report read.

It continued, "At least some of the influencers have been assigned to civilian roles that could lead to changes in policy, the people familiar with the matter said."

HEGSETH ANNOUNCES JOINT TASK FORCE WITH DOJ TO PROSECUTE LEAKS TO JOURNALISTS 'WITH THE FULL FORCE OF THE LAW'

After the article was published, Maness, Schlichter and Anderson pushed back on its implications, accusing the publication of using illegally obtained information to frame them as federal plants.

Each clarified that they were invited by the Department of War to take part as advisors in a task force studying senior service colleges through their military experience and past commentary on ways to improve the institutions. They added that they were previously compensated only for their roles in the task force, which has since concluded.

"My service with the Department of War as a 'Special Government Employee' was exclusively limited to participation in such task force and ended on July 26, 2026," Anderson, under the account "Cynical Publius," posted to X Sunday. "At no time have I ever received any compensation of any kind from any government source of any kind for anything I write or have ever written on X or in any magazine or other source. Those who claim otherwise defame me. I proudly and unabashedly support the efforts of President Trump and the Department of War because it’s the right thing to do."

FIRED STARS AND STRIPES STAFFERS SUE PENTAGON, ALLEGE RETALIATION AND FIRST AMENDMENT VIOLATION

Maness wrote on X Monday, "The Washington Post article published about me attempts to establish a context with its subtitle that is completely fabricated, categorically false, and defames me. The article also publishes illegally obtained personally identifiable information from government data sources about me. I patriotically and unashamedly support the efforts of President Trump, Secretary Hegseth, and the Department of War to ensure we are producing senior officers who can win our nation’s wars because it’s the most impactful thing to do for America’s future."

Schlichter published his own article critiquing The Washington Post in his column on Townhall.com on Monday.

"The leftists who seized on this innuendo don’t care about the truth, and it’s irrelevant whether the regime media reporters wrote garbage on purpose or because they are grossly incompetent. I don’t argue with people who, through malice or ineptitude, act in bad faith unless I’m in court. But I will use this situation as a cautionary example of why the regime media is trash and why your contempt for it is so well-deserved," Schlichter wrote, adding that the original piece misspelled his name.

HEGSETH EXCORIATES MEDIA, LIKENING THEM TO ‘PHARISEES’ IN TRUMP DEFENSE

In a comment to Fox News Digital, Post journalist Dan Lamothe said the article was "accurate as written" in that neither the journalists nor the Pentagon "disclosed they were special government employees" while they were commenting on Pentagon matters.

The Washington Post did not immediately respond to a request for additional comment.

When reached for a comment, the Pentagon pointed to a comment written by Under Secretary of War Anthony Tata on X Sunday.

"Senior officers deserve the best possible education: effective, unbiased & laser-focused on our core warfighting mission. @SecWar directed a Senior Service College Task Force to conduct a comprehensive review of @DeptofWar SSCs. Its mandate: ensure these institutions are anchored in military history, strategy, high standards, meritocracy & overall excellence. That review is now complete. Special thanks to @RobManess, @KurtSchlichter & Tom Anderson for answering the call to serve on this Task Force. Led by Dr. Maurice L. Todd—ASW(R), PhD, MA, MS & top 5% West Point graduate—they delivered critical recommendations to strengthen our SSCs & prepare our military leaders to achieve peace through strength," Tata wrote.

item.title: Ketel Marte booed in return to Arizona after declining to deliver a message to Diamondbacks fans
item.description: Ketel Marte was met with boos in his return to the Diamondbacks lineup against the Phillies after his unexplained absence during the playoff race.
item.content:encoded:
As the 2026 Major League Baseball season somehow draws to a close, one of the most bizarre and inexplicable stories is the saga of Arizona Diamondbacks star Ketel Marte.

Marte, long one of the best players in baseball and a pivotal part of a team pushing for a wild card spot, decided not to show up to a game between the Diamondbacks and Boston Red Sox at Fenway. He didn't tell anyone, including his teammates, manager, front office or coaching staff, that he wouldn't be at the ballpark. Didn't have a solid excuse ready, or a solid explanation, other than revealing a few days later that he was going for an MRI on his knee.

His manager, Torey Lovullo, admitted that he felt "betrayed" by Marte's absence, and his teammates were clear that they also did not appreciate the fact that he didn't show up. The Diamondbacks' front office was also disappointed, saying it was a "complete mystery" and that the entire incident was "bizarre."

KETEL MARTE'S UNEXPLAINED ABSENCE GETS STRANGER AS DIAMONDBACKS FIGHT FOR NL WILD CARD SPOT

Marte eventually met with Lovullo and team executives at Chase Field in Phoenix, apologizing for his behavior and reaffirming his commitment to the team. And on Monday night, he finally made his return to the dugout as the Diamondbacks start a big series against the Philadelphia Phillies.

Before the game, Marte answered questions from the media, including one in which he addressed how he'd handle speaking to the rest of the clubhouse.

DIAMONDBACKS STAR SPOTTED AT CASINO DURING TEAM'S GAME AFTER NO-SHOWING TO STADIUM EARLIER IN THE WEEK

"I'm going to stand in front of my teammates like a man," he said. "I'm going to ask for forgiveness. We're human, we all commit mistakes."

As for what happened to lead to Marte's unexcused absence? Well, that's still unclear.

"A moment of frustration," he explained. "No one made the decision for me, I'm the one that made the decision to not show up. I get along really well with Torey, and in that instance I failed him by not showing up," he added.

Given that Marte missed so much time during a playoff race, fans were always going to have a difficult time accepting his absence. He was asked about that too, whether he had a message for the Diamondbacks' fan base after what happened, but Marte shook his head without giving an explanation.

Well, those same fans clearly weren't thrilled about it. When Marte came up to the plate for his first at-bat, he was met with a chorus of boos. Boos that got louder after he grounded out in his first plate appearance.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

After the game, Marte explained that he hadn't understood the phrasing of the question asking what he'd like to say to the fans.

"Going back to the press conference, when the question was made to me, I didn’t really quite understand the word that was used at that moment," he said. "I’m never going to stop loving my fans, and that’s what I want them to understand."

English isn't Marte's first language, and he relies on an interpreter to talk to the media, so it's very possible he didn't fully understand the question. But his hat choice for postgame media availability raised some eyebrows and gave some cause to doubt whether that explanation was fully accurate.

"May the bridges I burn light the way" is certainly a choice for someone who missed two weeks' worth of games late in the season.

Marte has missed games in the past, and it's very possible that there are other mental health issues at work here, not to mention potential off-the-field problems. Supporting someone as they deal with off-field problems, personal issues, or other family concerns is part of fandom and sports in general. It’s hard, though, for fans to have grace when they aren’t given much explanation, justification or apology.

But if Marte leads Arizona back to the playoffs, all might be forgiven sooner rather than later.

item.title: Ted Cruz shuts down Trump Supreme Court talk with a fiery 'not just no, but hell no'
item.description: Sen. Ted Cruz told Sean Hannity his answer to a Supreme Court nomination from Trump would be "not just no, but hell no," despite his deep legal background.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, has dismissed speculation about a potential Supreme Court nomination, saying his response to President Donald Trump would be "not just no, but hell no."

Speaking on the "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast, Cruz said he would rather remain in politics than serve on the Supreme Court.

"So look, my answer is not just no, but hell no. And listen, I don't say that lightly. I mean, it’s a big deal. The court is an institution I revere," Cruz told Hannity.

ALITO NOT EXPECTED TO RETIRE THIS TERM, COOLING SUPREME COURT VACANCY SPECULATION: SOURCES

"And a lot of people are surprised, because I've spent an awful lot of my professional life around the court, in the court. And for so many people, it is their life dream to do," he added.

Trump has floated Cruz’s name for the Supreme Court in the past, joking he’d be the only nominee to get "100% of the Democrat vote, 100% of the Republican vote" because lawmakers would want to "get him out" of Congress.

TRUMP CHEERS ALITO STAYING FOR ANOTHER SUPREME COURT TERM: 'ONE OF THE GREATEST OF ALL TIME'

Before entering politics, Cruz graduated from Princeton University and got his law degree from Harvard Law School. After law school, he clerked for Chief Justice William Rehnquist and later worked in private practice.

During his conversation with Hannity, Cruz called Trump a "good friend," despite their rivalry during the 2016 Republican presidential primary. He also said that federal judges typically have to stay out of politics and policy battles.

SUPREME COURT CHIEF JUSTICE PINPOINTS WHAT AMERICANS MISUNDERSTAND ABOUT HIM AND HIS COLLEAGUES

"Because a principled federal judge stays out of politics and stays out of policy fights," Cruz said of why he would not want a seat on the bench.

Cruz was sworn into the Senate in 2013. He previously served as solicitor general of Texas from 2003 to 2008 and argued nine cases before the U.S. Supreme Court.

The Texas Tribune reported that Cruz was among 20 potential Supreme Court picks on Trump’s 2020 short list. Cruz responded to his inclusion on the list in a statement on X, then known as Twitter:

"I am grateful for the president’s confidence in me and for his leadership in nominating principled constitutionalists to the federal bench over the last four years," Cruz said.

"It’s humbling and an immense honor to be considered for the Supreme Court. The High Court plays a unique role in defending our Constitution, and there is no greater responsibility in public service than to support and defend the Constitution of the United States," he added.

At the time, Cruz said he had been "blessed to lead the fight to preserve our constitutional liberties" in the Senate and looked forward to continuing that work.

Fox News's Alexandra Koch contributed to this report.

item.title: Deadly mystery unfolds as canoeists are found unresponsive after midnight trip
item.description: Two canoeists launched onto California's Tomales Bay before midnight to see bioluminescence. By morning, a search-and-rescue team found both dead.
item.content:encoded:
Two canoeists were mysteriously found dead after setting out shortly before midnight on California's Tomales Bay, prompting an investigation. 

The Marin County Sheriff’s Office said the canoeists were found unresponsive Sunday.

Authorities have publicly identified only one of the two victims as San Francisco resident Casey Flynn Melia, 36.

NURSE IMPALED BY POLE DURING HIKE FORCED TO TREK 10 MILES FOR HELP: 'A FREAK THING'

The two individuals had been camping along Tomales Bay before setting out in a canoe shortly before midnight Saturday, according to officials.

"When the pair did not return the following morning, members of their camping party alerted emergency services via 9-1-1," a statement said.

"First responders immediately initiated a search-and-rescue operation."

After finding Melia's companion "unresponsive in the water," rescuers later located Melia, who was "unresponsive near Hog Island." 

US WARNS TRAVELERS TO AVOID PICTURESQUE COUNTRY AS SECURITY RAPIDLY WORSENS

Both were subsequently pronounced dead.

"A forensic post-mortem examination and routine toxicology testing are scheduled for later this week," the statement said.

"The official cause and manner of death remain pending, awaiting the final findings of a joint investigation conducted by the Marin County Sheriff’s Office, the USCG [United States Coast Guard] and the NPS [National Park Service]."

Officials added, "Because this remains an active investigation, no further details are available from the Coroner Division at this time."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Marin County Sheriff's Office for additional information.

Nighttime kayaking has become increasingly popular in the Point Reyes area as visitors take to the water after dark to see bioluminescence, according to the NPS.

The bay contains bioluminescent plankton that creates a blue-green glow in the water when disturbed. 

But officials warn that kayaking after dark requires extra caution and additional safety measures.

"While kayaking at night, it is essential that you remain visible to other boat traffic," NPS' website states.

"We strongly recommend the use of a working 360-degree light for all vessels, including kayaks and canoes."

The deaths come amid other recent tragedies involving visitors to national parks and remote wilderness areas.

Earlier this month, a 68-year-old French tourist died after his vehicle became stuck in mud in Death Valley National Park, prompting him to set out on foot.

In Australia, an 18-year-old hiker was found dead in dense bushland in Nattai National Park after an eight-day search.

item.title: Colin Kaepernick is right about the NFL's 'performative' racism campaign — but he's also a hypocrite
item.description: Colin Kaepernick calls Roger Goodell's 2020 racial justice video "so performative" and "disingenuous" in a new interview promoting his upcoming memoir.
item.content:encoded:
As part of an ongoing media blitz to promote his upcoming memoir, former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick dismissed the league’s condemnation of racism as "performative."

In an interview with NBC News, Kaepernick criticized NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell over a video he released in 2020 amid nationwide protests following George Floyd’s death.

"His response through that video was only because of pressure from players, not because it was altruistic," Kaepernick said.

COLIN KAEPERNICK TO RECEIVE MUHAMMAD ALI AWARD FOR FIGHTING 'RACIAL INJUSTICE'

In the video, Goodell said the NFL condemned "racism and the systematic oppression of Black people."

"[Goodell’s message was] so laughable, in my mind, and so disingenuous," Kaepernick continued. "We had been trying to address the issue that the NFL created with blackballing me for years. To come out and say we should have listened on the back of that — while I’m still actively trying to play in the NFL — it’s so performative."

Kaepernick is right.

The NFL’s social justice campaigns and messaging are performative. Painting "End Racism" in the end zones and approving "Black Lives Matter" on helmets were ways for the league to signal its virtue. They were public-relations decisions, perhaps even financial ones, designed to avoid potential backlash from sponsors and consumers.

ABDUL EL-SAYED DODGES 'RACIST NFL' CLAIM, CONTINUES DEFENDING COLIN KAEPERNICK

The fact that Goodell, or anyone else, felt obligated to announce that the NFL does not support racism and the systematic oppression of black people perfectly exemplifies the term "performative."

That said, Kaepernick is not the one to lecture anyone about fraudulent behavior.

The former quarterback has spent the past decade performing, pandering, and spreading propaganda. His entire claim to activism is fraudulent.

Most notably, Kaepernick participated in a Netflix docuseries in which he compared the NFL scouting combine to a slave auction.

"Before they put you on the field, teams poke, prod, and examine you. Searching for any defect that might affect your performance," Kaepernick narrated in Colin in Black & White. "No boundary respected. No dignity left intact. What they don't want you to understand is what's being established is a power dynamic."

The scene then shifts to one in which players transform into enslaved black men in shackles while white slave masters bid on them and whip them.

Meanwhile, Kaepernick continued trying to return to the NFL, despite comparing the process of entering the league to slavery. Imagine that.

He is no more honest than Goodell or the sports media figures who championed his campaign.

Kaepernick has not played in the NFL since 2016. He later filed a grievance accusing the league and its owners of colluding to keep him out. The case was settled in 2019, with neither side admitting wrongdoing.
